rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: 'It came from three moves you already made' (line 30), immediately before a bullet naming three moves (the delta note, the one-threat pick, the skill critique) in flowing prose, not a formatted bulleted sub-list. Kept as PASS: the rule's stated harm mechanism ('added item and reorder silently falsifies it... invisible to the author editing the list') presumes an itemized list an author edits item-by-item; editing this continuous three-clause sentence to add a fourth move would require rewriting the whole bullet, which is far more visible than editing a bulleted list, so the silent-drift risk the rule targets is materially weaker here. The numeral also does real scaffolding work for a three-part sentence that carries no bullet points of its own. 'One loop, three sizes' (bold lead, line 6) functions as a title/handle, not prose adjacent to a visible list; 'Same shape at three altitudes' immediately after pivots into a second claim (the map's four strands also share the shape) rather than purely re-tallying the first three.
